editorial:
Imagine if your favorite YouTuber existed back in the sixties. You follow David, a young guy who is pretty much a mess. He feels lost in life, so he decides to film everything he does. He treats his camera like a best friend, talking to it about his failed dates and his weird habits. It feels like you are peeking into someone's private life, and the vibe is very loose and honest. You will recognize a lot of the things David goes through, like trying too hard to be cool or just feeling bored with the world around you.

The acting feels super natural because it is meant to look like a home movie. While the pace is slow at times, that is kind of the point since it is just a guy living his life. If you like movies that feel like a real person's diary, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you should try to find it in the best quality possible. If you can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection or find a high-quality rental on Apple TV, it makes the grainy look feel more intentional and artistic. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: By the end, David realizes that filming his life is not actually fixing his problems. He spends the whole movie trying to find himself through a lens, but he stays just as confused as when he started. The movie ends with him still filming, showing that he is stuck in a loop. He does not get a big happy ending or a huge life change; he just keeps recording his days, accepting his own chaos.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vlogs, indie films, or character studies.
